_comment: Trust policy for edullm-dataset-publish — WHO may become the general-purpose publisher.
`ecs-tasks.amazonaws.com` only, the same shape as the validator, the ingest roles, and the
prm800k producer (all verified live 2026-07-31). AWS Batch runs its containers as ECS tasks, so
that principal is what a running job needs; no human session, no EC2 instance, and no other role
THIS IS THE ROLE WHERE THAT MATTERS MOST, and the reason is worth stating rather than inheriting.
This identity may write `dataset.json` and `manifest.json` under every one of the seven families
-- so it is the one role that can reserve a version and fire the validator for ANY dataset, not
just one corpus. The intern role in this account carries AdministratorAccess, so IAM is not what
keeps a human out of it; this trust policy is. Keeping it unassumable from a session is what
makes 'publishing happens only through a reviewed Batch job' a mechanism instead of a habit --
and it is why a broad grant here is acceptable in a way it would not be for a session-assumable
Deliberately NO `Condition` block, for the reason recorded on the ingest roles: Batch does not
populate `aws:SourceArn` on the ECS task-assume call the way one would expect, so a SourceArn
condition scoping this to one job queue evaluates false and every job fails to start with an
unhelpful credential error. The blast radius is bounded by the permission policy
(10-dataset-publish-policy.json): it Denies every write to edullm-data, every write to the
pipeline's own `_`-prefixed control prefixes, and any forged validator verdict.
